title: Meatloaf with Ketchup and Brown Sugar Glaze
changes_from_base: Topped with a cooked ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar and mustard glaze applied in two coats and finished under the grill, instead of the tomato purée top.
summary: This follows the same method as our classic meatloaf, but the top is finished with a cooked ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar and mustard glaze, brushed on in two coats and caramelised under the grill (broiler) instead of the tomato purée topping.
equipment: wire rack that fits the tray

ingredients.item: day-old white bread, crusts removed, torn small
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Cook the aromatics
steps.text: Warm the oil in the frying pan on a medium heat, then fry the onion for 6-8 minutes until it turns soft and lightly golden. Add the garlic and thyme for 1 minute, then leave to cool for 10 minutes, so the onion doesn't release raw moisture or crunch into the finished loaf.

steps.title: Mix the loaf
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Mash the bread and milk to a paste in the mixing bowl, beat in the eggs, then add the beef mince, cooled onions, parsley, soy sauce, salt and pepper. Mix with your hands only until evenly combined, as overmixing makes the loaf dense rather than tender.

steps.title: Shape on a holed rack
steps.text: Cover the wire rack with foil, poke holes through it every 2cm with a skewer, and set it on the tray. Shape the mixture on top into a loaf about 23 x 12cm; the holes let fat drain away and air reach every side, so the loaf browns evenly rather than stewing.

steps.title: Make the glaze
steps.text: Simmer the ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar and mustard powder together in the small saucepan for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until thick and glossy. Cooking the glaze down first concentrates it, so it clings to the loaf instead of running straight off.

steps.title: Bake with two coats of glaze
steps.text: Bake the loaf for 45 minutes, then brush over half the glaze and bake for a further 15 minutes. Brush on the remaining glaze and bake for another 5-15 minutes, until a probe thermometer in the centre reads 71°C — two thinner coats build a thicker, glossier layer than one.

steps.title: Lacquer under the grill
steps.text: Switch the oven to a high grill (broiler) setting and grill the loaf for 2-3 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze bubbles and darkens at the edges. Rest for 10 minutes so it firms up and slices cleanly, then cut into 2cm slices.

tips: Watch the loaf closely under the grill — the sugar in the glaze can catch and burn in well under a minute if you step away.
Brush the glaze on in two thin coats rather than one thick one; it builds a better sheen and clings more evenly.
Mix the meat gently and only until combined, since this is the step most likely to leave the loaf tough rather than tender.
Confirm 71°C at the centre with a probe thermometer before relying on the glaze colour alone, as a dark glaze can form before the middle is fully cooked.
storage: Keeps in a sealed container in the fridge for up to 3 days, or sliced and frozen for up to 3 months. Reheat slices in a covered dish in the oven, or in the microwave, until piping hot throughout (74°C). Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
